habit_scope: cold climates / East–Midwest (HUD RSDG §4.1; ORNL BFH §1.3). Wasatch + Logan regional habit (30 in frost). Fontana: not the Southern habit.
how_it_is_done: Site: pick the high/dry spot if the site is wet; confirm water table; test hole; stakes; strip topsoil; protect trees/utilities; winter frost protection for open work (ORNL BFH §2.4 SITEWORK). Compact fill and stripped-root zones before footings (AF&PA Details, Foundations).

Termite prep (ongoing): pull roots, stumps, scrap, and form stakes from the foundation area (ORNL §§2.2/3.2/4.2; AF&PA Termites). Soil termiticide where termites are a hazard. Do not disturb treated soil before the slab pour (ORNL checklist). Do not trade treatment for shields (D8 / c-P05-D8-termite-shields).

Footings below local frost, or insulated FPSF if that engineered/IRC alt is chosen (HUD §4.8; ORNL §2.2). Do not pour on frozen ground; do not fill an over-excavated trench; do not bear half-on-rock (ORNL FOOTINGS). Width from soil bearing; equipment buckets 12/16/24 in (HUD §4.4). Thickness ≈ wall thickness and ≈ projection (AF&PA rule of thumb; HUD §4.4: thickness ≥ projection and ≥6 in, projection ≥2 in). Optional two No. 4/No. 5 bars near top. Keyway or dowels to wall (ORNL note 19). Concrete typically 2500 psi (ORNL) or 2500–3000 psi (HUD §4.2); slump 4–6 in; add no water on site.

Walls: CIP or CMU. Local contractor skill and material yards often decide CIP vs CMU more than physics (ORNL §1.3) — keep both in this method. CMU: parge, then dampproof/asphalt; solid cap or bond beam or grouted top course (AF&PA Concrete Foundations; ORNL notes 6, 22, 31, 33). CIP: plug form-tie holes before waterproofing; cure (ORNL checklist). Unreinforced 8-in CIP ≤7 ft fill or 12-in CMU ≤6 ft fill in stable, low-seismic soil (ORNL notes 14, 22); otherwise engineer / IRC tables (HUD §4.5). Wasatch seismic D2 is a reason tables may not be enough — engineer when tables fail, not a stamp.

Dampproof vs waterproof (see m-P05-waterproof): dampproof + poly for vapor; waterproof if finished basement, poor drainage, or hydrostatic (ORNL §2.2). Waterproof on the wall, insulation outboard of it, down to the footing drain (ORNL note 6).

Subdrain: 4-in perf pipe, holes down, 1 in in 20 ft, gravel envelope, filter fabric, to daylight or sump; clean-out; never connect roof leaders (ORNL note 8). AF&PA: drain tile around the entire CIP/block footing. Not used with PWF (D9).

Basement slab: 4 in min (ORNL note 16; HUD §4.6 ACI 302). 6-mil poly, 12-in laps. Isolation joint at wall; slab floats — do not sit it on a wall ledge (ORNL note 16 / Ch 4 ACI/BRAB; D6 / c-P05-D6-slab-bearing). WWF or fibers for shrinkage / radon where called. Cure ~3 days at 70°F (ORNL radon). Soil treatment already done; form wood out of the pour.

Backfill / grade: porous backfill or drainage mat; compact; 5% slope away (6 in in 10 ft); gutters (ORNL notes 2–4). Waterproofing before backfill. Floor framing must exist to brace the top of basement walls before significant backfill (HUD §4.5 simple-span model) — m-P07-* PRECEDES significant basement backfill, can_overlap false.

Sill: treated, ≥8 in above grade, inspectable (ORNL; AF&PA 8 in framing / 6 in siding). Bolts ½ in, ~6 ft o.c., ≤1 ft from corners (ORNL notes 13/31; AF&PA ~6 ft). Embed: D2 / c-P05-D2-sill-bolt-embed — follow adopted code; 15 in masonry is the high-wind/uplift variant.
trades: ORNL checklist: grading contractor, construction contractor, landscape contractor for grade definitions
AF&PA: job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector — no crew size
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources. Named: excavator bucket widths 12/16/24 in (HUD §4.4); wall forms; form stakes (must come out before termite/slab).
inspection_hold_points: Footing inspection before pour; no frozen subgrade (ORNL).
Wall forms, steel, and bolt layout before pour; no extra water (ORNL / HUD §4.2).
Waterproofing before backfill; protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
Soil treatment before slab; form wood out of the pour (ORNL).
Floor framing in before significant backfill of basement walls (HUD §4.5).

ORNL Fig 1-4 last step: establish QC inspection procedures; Ch 2 checklists dual-use design and field. AF&PA: inspector enforces the illustrated procedures. HUD: IRC so builder + official can inspect without a PE; PE when tables fail.
Radon standpipe in subslab gravel, cap, preferably stack through roof during construction (ORNL §2.2 only — not in AF&PA or HUD RSDG). Med confidence; regional.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit in cold climates / East–Midwest and on Wasatch/Logan (30 in frost). ORNL §1.3: MN-style frost depth makes half the wall already required. Walkout combo (basement uphill + slab downhill) is normal on slopes (ORNL §1.3) — same method, not a new type.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Veto if water table within ~8 ft (ORNL §1.3) — use crawl or slab. Not the Fontana / South-Southwest habit. Unreinforced wall limits exceeded (ORNL notes 14, 22) without engineer / IRC tables. Piles/helical are not this method (c-P05-piles-not-inland-habit).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did learn it — this is the cold-climate / East–Midwest basement habit. CIP vs CMU follows the local yard, not a new skill.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Foundation type on drawings before permit. Engineer when IRC tables fail (HUD) or unreinforced wall limits exceeded (ORNL notes 14, 22). Sill bolt schedule / shear later is P08. FPSF if used is engineered/IRC-prescriptive, still not a separate method.
risk_if_swapped_late: Swapping basement vs slab/crawl after permit is a type change: excavation depth, waterproofing, drain tile, floor package, and stairs all move. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: In cold country this is the usual basement: poured wall or block on a spread footing, bottom of footing below frost. Waterproof and put drain tile on before you backfill. Do not dump dirt against the walls until the first-floor framing is on to brace the top. CIP or block is whichever the local yard pours or lays.
spanish_summary: En clima frío el hábito es sótano de concreto colado o block sobre zapata corrida, con el fondo debajo de la helada. Se impermeabiliza y se pone drenaje antes de rellenar. No rellene fuerte las paredes hasta que el piso de madera esté armado. Colado o block lo decide el patio local.

fastener_schedule.pattern: through treated sill into wall (CIP/CMU, crawl wall, or slab stem/edge)
fastener_schedule.source: ORNL notes 13/31; AF&PA Sills. Embed D2 both variants (AF&PA ≥6 in CIP / ≥15 in block vs ORNL most codes ≥7 in / some 15 in masonry for uplift) — follow AHJ. Do not pick a winner.
